description:
Thick smoke from wildfires in Canada is once again blanketing major US cities, including Chicago, Detroit, and New York, which now have some of the worst air quality in the world. 

Some Republican lawmakers have blamed Canada for failing to prevent the fires. But ultimately the blame should fall on a much bigger force that’s making smoky summers part of America’s new normal. #Wildfires #ClimateChange #airquality

author: Vox
description:
Why does Odysseus sound like he’s from Ohio?

Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey gives its ancient Greek heroes American accents, breaking a long Hollywood tradition of making the ancient world sound British. The choice raises a bigger question. Why have we spent decades assuming kings, empires, and fantasy worlds should sound a certain way? This video explores how British accents became Hollywood’s shorthand for power, from classic epics to Star Wars and Gladiator. If those accents once represented power, what should power sound like now? #Odyssey #movies

author: Vox
description:
What makes a candidate electable in today’s Democratic Party? Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed tells Vox’s Astead Herndon why he believes the traditional left-right spectrum no longer explains American politics. Instead, he argues, voters are divided between people who feel locked out of power and those doing the locking out.

author: Vox
description:
AI was supposed to make our lives better. Instead, it’s made many of us scared and angry. Communities are protesting data centers across the country, and polling shows most Americans think AI is moving too fast.

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In today's episode, guest host Miles Bryan talks with independent journalist Jasmine Sun, who argues that public attitudes toward AI are undergoing a fundamental shift. Jasmine argues that AI is seen not simply as a technology to adopt, but as an elite political project to resist. The two discuss “AI populism,” the parallels with the Industrial Revolution, how public opinion about AI may affect US politics, and how the leaders of Silicon Valley are unprepared for the growing backlash against AI.

Guest Host: Miles Bryan, Vox reporter and senior producer
Guest:Jasmine Sun, journalist
